answer: We formulate a consensus protocol over a cryptographic trellis graph, binding dynamic opportunity-cost staking collateral to zero-knowledge verifiable delay proofs. Integrating physical pigment entropy into state assertions creates an expected-utility ridge that enforces quadratic capital barriers against identity multiplication. A subgame-perfect slashing matrix guarantees that the expected attack utility E[U(k)] of generating k Sybil nodes remains strictly negative. Thus, single-identity commitment achieves a strict Nash equilibrium in adversarial multi-agent environments.
